draft:
Hi Ryan,

Thanks for getting in touch - happy to help clarify the error your users are encountering.

The error "Document limit has been reached" occurs when the S-Docs document generation entitlement for your organization has been exhausted. This is typically due to one of the following reasons:

1. Your organization is on the free edition of S-Docs, which is limited to generating 150 documents. Once this cap is reached, document generation will stop until the entitlement is increased.
2. If your organization is using a legacy version of S-Docs (prior to the Fall '24 / 8.0 release) that relies on license keys, the key may be missing or expired, causing the system to revert to free-edition limits.

To resolve this issue:

1. Confirm which S-Docs edition your organization is using. The free edition has the 150-document limit, while paid editions allow unlimited document generation.
2. If your organization is on the free edition and has hit the cap, upgrading to a paid S-Docs edition is required to continue generating documents. If you'd like assistance with this, let us know.
3. If your organization runs a legacy version of S-Docs and you have a new or renewed license key, you can install it as follows:
   
   - Navigate to App Launcher > S-Docs Templates.
   - Open the License Key template.
   - Click "Edit," delete the text in the Document Version field, and replace it with the new license key.
   - Save the changes. If successful, the field will display "***KEY ACCEPTED***."

If you'd like us to verify your current usage against your entitlement or need further assistance, please reply with your Salesforce org ID, and we’d be happy to help.

Let us know if you have any further questions or need additional support!

You may also find these resources helpful:
- S-Docs error: SDCreate3 initialization error: Document limit has been reached: https://kb.sdocs.com/faq/

Happy to hop on a call if that's easier - just let me know a couple of times that suit you and I'll get something on the calendar.

Hi Norman,

Thanks for getting in touch - happy to help you migrate your S-Docs templates from sandbox to production in Salesforce!

You can migrate templates using either of the following methods:

**1. Single Template Export/Import:**
This method is recommended if you are migrating fewer than 15 templates.

1. Open the source template in the S-Docs Template Editor.
2. Navigate to the "Advanced Options" tab and click "Export Template."
3. Click "Generate" to produce a string of importable template data (DOCX attachments and S-Sign data are included if applicable).
4. Copy the generated string and save it in a plain text file.
5. In the target org, go to the App Launcher > S-Docs > Templates tab > New.
6. Enter a name for the new template and click "Save." (Fields entered here will be overridden on import.)
7. On the template detail page, open the Template Editor.
8. Paste the exported template data into the Template Body tab and click "Save." The system will decode the data and populate all template fields automatically.

**2. Bulk Migration Using the S-Docs Template Migrator:**
This method is best for migrating multiple templates.

1. Ensure your S-Docs version is 4.210+ and S-Sign version is 2.78+ if migrating S-Sign-enabled templates.
2. Open the Template Migrator:
   - For S-Docs 4.381+, go to App Launcher > S-Docs Setup > "Migrate S-Docs & S-Sign Templates" > Go To S-Docs Migration Page.
   - For earlier versions, append `/apex/SDOC__SDMigrate` to your Salesforce URL.
3. Use SOQL filters to select templates, then click "Set Export Filters."
4. Select templates to export using the checkboxes, then click "Generate Export Zip." Avoid exporting templates named "License Key" or "License Data."
5. In the target org, upload the .zip file on the migration page by clicking "Choose File" and selecting the file.
6. Optionally check "Set SDOC Template Values?" to modify field data on import, then click "Start Import."

**Important Notes:**
- After migration, ensure that any references to sandbox-specific data (e.g., image URLs or sandbox-hosted assets) are updated to production equivalents.
- If custom fields, objects, or record types are used in the templates, ensure these exist in the target org with matching API names and configurations.

Let us know if you need help with any of these steps or encounter any issues during the migration process!

You may also find these resources helpful:
- Clone S-Docs templates and migrate templates between orgs (sandbox to production: https://kb.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/managing-templates/moving-templates-from-sandbox-to-production/
- Template Lifecycle Management: https://help.sdocs.com/sdocs/template-architecture/template-settings/advanced-options-tab/template-lifecycle-management

Happy to hop on a call if that's easier - just let me know a couple of times that suit you and I'll get something on the calendar.

Hi Syam,

Thanks for getting in touch - happy to help with the S-Docs license expired error you're seeing.

To resolve this issue, you'll need to renew the license key using the following steps:

1. Open S-Docs in your Salesforce environment.
2. Navigate to S-Docs Templates.
3. Locate the "License Key" template. If you don't see it, switch to "All Inactive Templates" to find it.
4. Open the "License Key" template record and click "Edit."
5. Paste the new license key into the "Document Version" field.
6. Save the record.

Once the update is successful, you should see "***KEY ACCEPTED***" displayed in the "Document Version" field.

If users still encounter issues editing templates after this, ensure they have read access to the "License Key" template. You can achieve this by creating a sharing rule on the S-Docs Template object for the relevant users.

Let us know if you need assistance with retrieving the new license key, creating the sharing rule, or if you encounter any other issues!

Happy to hop on a call if that's easier - just let me know a couple of times that suit you and I'll get something on the calendar.

Hi there,

Thanks for getting in touch - happy to help with the issue of blank documents being generated in S-Docs.

When S-Docs generates blank documents, the most common cause is related to merge fields not populating correctly. Here are a few steps to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. Open the affected S-Docs Template and check the <<field>> tokens used in the template. Ensure that the field API names match the corresponding fields in the base object.
2. Verify that the relationship path for the fields resolves correctly from the base object specified in the template.
3. Confirm that the field-level security settings in Salesforce allow visibility for the fields being used in the template.
4. Ensure that the "Related-To" object in the template matches the record from which you are generating the document.

If you have already checked these points and the issue persists, feel free to provide additional details or let us know if you'd like to arrange a meeting to demonstrate the issue further. We're here to assist!

Looking forward to your reply if you need further help!
